t: Chandragupta rose in the unrest that followed Alexander the Great's Indian campaign, defeated the Nanda dynasty in Magadha and founded the Maurya Empire, though the order and dates of these events remain debated.

He made a dynastic marriage alliance with Seleucus I Nicator c. 305–303 BCE, receiving the regions along the Indus and sending 500 elephants in exchange, and ruled through a decentralised administration of provinces and local governments.

His life reaches us only through Greek and Roman fragments and Hindu, Buddhist and Jain texts written centuries later, which disagree on his origins, his rise and his death, so historians treat most of the narrative with caution.
dyk: Sir William Jones proposed in 1793 that the Indian king "Sandracottus" of the Greek and Roman writers was Chandragupta of the Sanskrit texts, which made it possible to match Indian and Graeco-Roman history; his reign has been called "the sheet anchor of Indian chronology".
ev: Alexander the Great ends his Indian campaign in 326 to 325 BCE; Plutarch later claims that Chandragupta, as a young man, saw him
Alexander dies in Babylon and war breaks out between his generals, leaving unrest in the Indian territories he had assigned to Greek governors
Chandragupta's conquest of Magadha and the defeat of the Nandas is generally dated between 322 and 319 BCE, though a later chronology places it c. 311–305 BCE
Jansari dates Chandragupta's arrival in the Punjab here, in line with the chronology of Greek history
Chandragupta and Seleucus I Nicator confront each other and then, by about 303 BCE, form a dynastic marriage alliance
According to Roy, Chandragupta's abdication may be dated here
According to Roy, Chandragupta dies at some point between 297 and 293 BCE

f.born: Year and place unknown; there are no historical facts about his origins and early life, only legends. The year given here, c. 320 BCE, is the conventional start of his reign. Greek and Roman, Hindu, Buddhist and Jain sources give differing accounts of his family
f.died: Date, place and circumstances unclear and disputed; according to Roy, he abdicated c. 298 BCE and died between 297 and 293 BCE. Digambara Jain tradition says he fasted to death at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka, a story that Sushma Jansari calls late and problematic
f.role: Founder and first emperor of the Maurya Empire, based in Magadha; reigned c. 320 BCE – c. 298 BCE (scholars give dates from 324 or 322 to 297 or 293 BCE)
f.known: overthrowing the Nanda dynasty and founding the Maurya Empire; the war against Alexander's Greek governors in the Indus Valley; the marriage alliance and exchange of 500 elephants with Seleucus I Nicator; a decentralised administration with provinces and a council of advisers; irrigation works and roads; his partnership with Chanakya in the legends; the Jain story of his renunciation
